summary: Lemmy is a self-hosted link aggregator and discussion platform that operates within the fediverse. It functions as an alternative to centralised forums like Reddit, allowing users to create communities, post links, and participate in threaded conversations across interconnected servers.
goodFor: This software is well-suited for groups or individuals wanting to run an independent discussion forum that can federate with other instances on the ActivityPub network.
watchOut: Federated software requires active moderation to handle spam and unwanted traffic from other instances on the network. It also faces the challenge of building an active user base compared to established mainstream platforms.
deployNotes: As a containerised application, it typically requires persistent storage volumes for database and media files, alongside a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination.
